acceptance_criteria.criterion: The class compiles without errors and follows project conventions (declare(strict_types=1), array() syntax, no constructor promotion).
getMethodName() correctly converts underscore-separated IDs to camelCase.
getFullIconName() returns prefix:iconName when prefix is non-empty, otherwise just iconName.
createIcon() returns a UI_Icon with the correct type set (one-arg call when prefix is empty, two-arg call otherwise).
isCustom() and isStandard() return mutually exclusive boolean values matching the $isCustom constructor argument.

summary: Created src/classes/UI/Icons/IconInfo.php — a read-only value object in the UI\Icons namespace. Constructor accepts id, iconName, prefix, and isCustom flag. Provides all specified getters, createIcon() (one-arg setType() when prefix is empty, two-arg otherwise), getMethodName() (underscore-to-camelCase conversion), and getFullIconName() (prefix:iconName or just iconName). Follows all project conventions: declare(strict_types=1), array() syntax, no constructor promotion, no readonly. PHPStan passes with no errors. composer dump-autoload completed successfully.

comments.note: No observations — the new file is a small, clean value object with no coupling concerns. Code in the touched files is clean and consistent.

summary: All five acceptance criteria verified independently through code review and test execution. PHPStan reports zero errors on the new file (single pre-existing error in DBHelper/FetchMany.php is unrelated). Existing IconsTest (2 tests) passes with no regressions. Logic trace confirms: getMethodName() correctly produces camelCase (attention_required → attentionRequired); getFullIconName() correctly returns prefix:name or bare name; createIcon() uses one-arg vs two-arg setType() appropriately (confirmed against UI_Icon::setType signature which accepts optional prefix defaulting to 'fa'); isCustom()/isStandard() are mathematically mutually exclusive.

comments.note: getMethodName() with an empty string ID returns an empty string (explode('_','') yields [''], array_shift returns ''). This is harmless in practice since icon IDs are non-empty strings sourced from JSON, but there is no guard. No action needed for this WP scope.

PHP empty() returns true for the string '0', so a prefix value of '0' would be treated as empty in createIcon(). FontAwesome prefixes are always alphabetic identifiers (far, fab, fas), so this is a non-issue in practice.

No PHPUnit test class for IconInfo was created. The AC does not require one, and the logic is fully verifiable by code review. A dedicated test class (e.g. tests/AppFrameworkTests/UI/IconInfoTest.php) would add value in a future WP.
